methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort (2008-2020, n=1290: 307 OBCS, 983 lumpectomy) comparing oncoplastic breast-conserving surgery vs standard lumpectomy. Appropriate statistical testing (t-tests for continuous, chi-square for categorical comparisons). Clear definitions of complications (wound infection, dehiscence, fat necrosis). Kaplan-Meier for recurrence-free survival. Limitations: retrospective design, younger age in OBCS group (56 vs 61 years), treatment assignment bias inherent.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort study (LoE 2b) demonstrating equivalent oncologic outcomes (recurrence, DFS) and safety profile for OBCS vs standard lumpectomy despite minor wound complications. Directly informs shared decision-making regarding surgical approach in breast-conserving therapy.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE-aligned observational reporting: patient flow (1880 screened, 1290 analyzed), baseline characteristics, treatment details, complications systematically documented, oncologic outcomes clearly presented. Limitations: retrospective methodology; incomplete long-term follow-up for some patients; no data repository statement.

novelty_literature.justification: Large long-term breast-conserving surgery outcomes comparison (n=1290, 12-year follow-up); OBCS increasingly used but large comparative effectiveness studies limited. Demonstrates safety/equivalence enabling broader OBCS adoption.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized breast surgery comparative effectiveness study with clear clinical motivation (OBCS safety/cosmetic benefit concerns). Methods, results, complications systematically presented. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings for clinical practice impact.

key_strengths: Large single-center cohort (n=1290) with 12-year follow-up demonstrating equivalent oncologic outcomes (recurrence, DFS, margin status, mastectomy conversion) between OBCS and standard lumpectomy

Systematically documented complications with clear definition and frequency reporting: minor complications higher in OBCS (infection 7.17% vs 3.66%, dehiscence 4.89% vs 0.92%, fat necrosis 11.73% vs 1.12%) but manageable
Identifies modest radiotherapy delay (3.93 vs 3.57 months) without oncologic consequence, addressing clinical concern about treatment delays
Supports OBCS as safe breast-conserving option enabling improved cosmetic outcomes without compromising cancer control
key_concerns: Retrospective design with treatment selection bias; younger age in OBCS group (mean 56 vs 61 years) may represent inherent selection toward better-prognosis patients
Single-center origin limits generalizability; no external validation cohort; variability in OBCS techniques across surgeons not analyzed
Complication definitions limited to early wound healing issues; longer-term quality-of-life/esthetic outcomes not systematically assessed despite being study motivation
Missing data on cosmetic satisfaction, patient preference, return to normal activities despite these being key drivers of OBCS adoption
chief_reviewer.rationale: Large single-center retrospective study demonstrating OBCS oncologic safety and acceptance for breast-conserving therapy. Appropriate for tier 3 specialty journals after addressing external validation and quality-of-life outcome gaps.
